subject: Galileo - tenant-scoped log retention carveout request
messages:
From: Ari Patel <ari@galileohealthtech.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@galileohealthtech.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Tenant-scoped log retention carveout for Galileo prod tenant

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final stages of our SOC 2 audit and the auditor flagged that our retention requirement for certain transaction-level request logs needs to be 18 months for compliance with a legacy federal subcontract. Redwood's default tenant log TTL is 90 days, and we understand the platform standard.

We'd like to request a tenant-scoped carveout to extend retention of the following items to 18 months for our prod tenant only (galileo-prod):
- request-access logs (headers + route)
- system error traces (stack + kv for debugging)
- request metadata (timestamp, model, latency)

Constraints and asks from our side:
1) The extended logs must be stored encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys (we can provide KMS ARN).
2) Access should be limited via RBAC and logged to a separate audit trail.
3) We need an implementation timeline: ideally completed prior to our auditor re-check on Feb 10.
4) Please provide a short attestation/statement we can submit to the auditor that explains how Redwood will isolate the retention change to our tenant.

I've attached a small sample extract of the log subset we need to preserve. Happy to jump on a quick call — Laura (cc) is our security lead.

Appreciate it,
Ari
Security & Compliance
Galileo HealthTech

Attachment: galileo_log-sample.csv

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Ari Patel <ari@galileohealthtech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-15T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Tenant-scoped log retention carveout for Galileo prod tenant

Hi Ari — thanks for the clear summary and the sample. Looping in Neha (legal/compliance) and Vanessa (Customer Success) so we can coordinate the timeline and controls. Quick confirmations from our side:

- We can implement tenant-scoped retention overrides as a policy layer in Redwood Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we typically require a contractual amendment.
- We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we can integrate with customer KMS in some regions (need legal review).

Neha — can you confirm what we need on the attestation language and whether a contract amendment (SLA/Appendix) will be necessary for Hosted customers?

Vanessa — can you propose an ops timeline and any rollout/verification steps (snapshot, sample exports for auditor)? Ari is aiming for Feb 10. If we can't meet that, let's give a realistic date and an interim mitigation statement for the auditor.

I'll draft an initial carveout proposal once we have legal signoff.

Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Ari Patel <ari@galileohealthtech.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@galileohealthtech.com>
Date: 2026-01-16T08:23:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Request: Tenant-scoped log retention carveout for Galileo prod tenant

Stephanie / Vanessa / Ari — quick legal/compliance notes: 

1) For Hosted customers we generally require an addendum that specifies: scope of the data type subject to extended retention, duration, KMS controls, access limitations, and termination behavior (what happens at contract end). If Galileo is willing to sign an appendix, we can proceed without a full platform change request.

2) Attestation language: we can provide a short signed letter on company letterhead that describes the technical controls and the fact the change is tenant-scoped. Template items: description of the logs retained, retention window (18 months), encryption details (CMK ARN), RBAC controls, and a statement that the change is reversible and limited to galileo-prod.

3) Evidence deliverables auditors typically accept: a configuration snapshot (policy + keys), a sample export demonstrating 9+ months of preserved logs, access-control audit trail, and screenshots of the TTL policy bound to the tenant.

4) Timeline: legal can review and sign a standard appendix in ~5 business days once we have the exact policy text. Ops work (Vanessa) will be the gating factor for the Feb 10 ask.

I will draft the attestation template and a minimal appendix for Hosted customers. Ari — please confirm whether Galileo is Hosted or Dedicated/Private. That will change the implementation path.

-Neha
Lead Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
To: Ari Patel <ari@galileohealthtech.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-19T10:36:00-08:00
Subject: Proposed carveout + rollout plan (draft) — Galileo prod tenant

Ari / Laura — attaching a draft proposal (redwood-proposed-carveout-20260119.pdf) and SIG matrix excerpt for your records. Summary below: 

Proposed scope (tenant: galileo-prod):
- Retain request-access logs, error traces, and request metadata for 18 months (calendar days).
- Logs stored in a segregated retention bucket encrypted with customer CMK (Galileo KMS ARN required).
- Access controls: only roles with "audit.read" or "sre.debug" can read the extended-retention bucket; all access is logged to an immutable audit trail with its own retention of 3 years.
- Decommission: on contract termination or written request, Redwood will provide a certified deletion report and a final snapshot export.

Rolling out:
- Stage (2 days): create tenant policy, validate encryption, and create sample exports.
- Canaries (2 days): route a subset of traffic to extended retention and validate size/perf impact.
- Production (1 day): enable fully for galileo-prod.

Estimated calendar timeline: 7 business days from final KMS ARN + appendix signature. If Galileo provides the CMK ARN and signs the appendix by Jan 22, we can hit Feb 3 — earlier than your auditor re-check. If you need Feb 10 hard, we should still be fine but we'd like confirmation by Jan 24.

Deliverables for auditor:
- Signed appendix (legal)
- Attestation letter (Neha will sign)
- Configuration snapshot + sample export (Vanessa will deliver)

Questions for you:
1) Will Galileo provide an ARN for a customer-managed KMS?
2) Do you require the logs to be searchable (indexing) or just preserved as archived objects? Indexing has additional cost and latency implications; we can scope that separately.

Thanks — happy to hop on 20 minutes to finalize wording.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-proposed-carveout-20260119.pdf, sig-matrix-galileo.xlsx

From: Ari Patel <ari@galileohealthtech.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@galileohealthtech.com>, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2026-01-20T16:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposed carveout + rollout plan (draft) — Galileo prod tenant

Stephanie — this looks good and very thorough. Quick answers: 

- We are a Hosted customer.
- We will provide a CMK ARN by Jan 22.
- Indexing is not required for the audit; preserved archived objects are fine for now. If we need quick search later we'll scope indexing separately.

Laura and I reviewed the draft timeline and Feb 3 would be ideal — we'll aim to get the appendix signed by Jan 22. If anything slips we'll keep you posted, but appreciate the clear deliverables list for the auditor.

One small ask: can the attestation include the sample export filename format and a hash/checksum so our auditor can verify integrity?

Thanks again — Ari
Security & Compliance
Galileo HealthTech
